name: D&D 5e Reference (SRD 5.1)
description: Keyword-triggered reference for D&D 5e classes, conditions, sample spells, and core rules. Sourced from Wizards of the Coast's SRD 5.1, licensed CC-BY-4.0.

entries.name: XP Progression Mode
entries.content:
Progression: xp

(The line above is the campaign's progression switch — follow whichever mode it declares. 'Progression: xp' = the GM awards XP per the XP Awards entry's guidelines. 'Progression: milestone' = the GM awards NO XP, ever; the player triggers level-ups manually at the table's discretion. Players: edit only the first line to change modes.)

entries.name: Class: Fighter
entries.content: Fighter class. Hit Die: d10. Proficiencies: all armor, all shields, all weapons; STR + CON saves. At level 1 the Fighter gets Second Wind (bonus action: regain 1d10 + level HP, once per short rest) and a chosen Fighting Style. At level 2: Action Surge (one extra action on a turn, once per short rest). At level 5: Extra Attack (attack twice with the Attack action).

entries.name: Class: Wizard
entries.content: Wizard class. Hit Die: d6. Proficiencies: daggers, darts, slings, quarterstaffs, light crossbows; INT + WIS saves. Spellcasting: prepares wizard spells from a spellbook each long rest, slots 1st-9th level. Arcane Recovery (once/day on short rest): recover spell slots totaling at most half your wizard level (rounded up), no slot 6th or higher. Ritual Casting: any prepared spell with the ritual tag can be cast as a ritual.

entries.name: Class: Rogue
entries.content: Rogue class. Hit Die: d8. Proficiencies: light armor; simple weapons, hand crossbows, longswords, rapiers, shortswords; DEX + INT saves; thieves' tools; four chosen skills (Expertise on two at level 1). Sneak Attack: 1d6 extra damage at level 1 (scales) on a hit when you have advantage or an ally adjacent and don't have disadvantage; once per turn. Cunning Action (level 2): bonus action to Dash, Disengage, or Hide.

entries.name: Class: Cleric
entries.content: Cleric class. Hit Die: d8. Proficiencies: light + medium armor + shields; simple weapons; WIS + CHA saves. Spellcasting (WIS): prepares cleric spells daily equal to WIS_mod + cleric level, plus all domain spells always prepared. Divine Domain at level 1 with first Channel Divinity at level 2 (use 1/short rest, scales to 2 at level 6, 3 at level 18).

entries.name: Condition: Prone
entries.content: Prone: A prone creature's only movement option is to crawl, unless it stands up (costing half its movement). It has disadvantage on attack rolls. An attack roll against a prone creature has advantage if the attacker is within 5 ft, and disadvantage otherwise.

entries.name: Condition: Grappled
entries.content: Grappled: Speed becomes 0 and cannot benefit from any bonus to speed. Ends if the grappler is incapacitated, or if an effect removes the grappled creature from the grappler's reach (such as being thrown).

entries.name: Condition: Poisoned
entries.content: Poisoned: Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

entries.name: Condition: Frightened
entries.content: Frightened: Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of fear is in line of sight. Cannot willingly move closer to the source.

entries.name: Spell: Fire Bolt (cantrip)
entries.content: Fire Bolt — Evocation cantrip. Casting Time: 1 action. Range: 120 ft. Components: V, S. Duration: instantaneous. Hurl a mote of fire at a creature or object in range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, target takes 1d10 fire damage. A flammable object hit by this spell ignites if it isn't being worn or carried. Damage scales: 2d10 at level 5, 3d10 at 11, 4d10 at 17.

entries.name: Spell: Cure Wounds (1st)
entries.content: Cure Wounds — Evocation 1st level. Casting Time: 1 action. Range: Touch. Components: V, S. Duration: instantaneous. A creature you touch regains hit points equal to 1d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier. No effect on undead or constructs. At higher levels: +1d8 per slot level above 1st.

entries.name: Spell: Shield (1st)
entries.content: Shield — Abjuration 1st level. Casting Time: 1 reaction, taken when you are hit by an attack or targeted by magic missile. Range: self. Components: V, S. Duration: 1 round. +5 bonus to AC, including against the triggering attack, and you take no damage from magic missile.

entries.name: Spell: Fireball (3rd)
entries.content: Fireball — Evocation 3rd level. Casting Time: 1 action. Range: 150 ft. Components: V, S, M (a tiny ball of bat guano and sulfur). Duration: instantaneous. A 20-ft-radius sphere of flame at a point in range. Each creature in the area makes a DEX save (DC = spell save DC). Failed save: 8d6 fire damage. Successful save: half. Ignites unattended flammable objects. At higher levels: +1d6 per slot above 3rd.

entries.name: Rule: Advantage / Disadvantage
entries.content: Advantage: roll the d20 twice, use the higher result. Disadvantage: roll the d20 twice, use the lower result. If both apply, they cancel — roll once normally. Multiple sources of advantage or disadvantage do not stack; presence of any advantage and any disadvantage cancels.

entries.name: Rule: Short and Long Rest
entries.content: Short rest: at least 1 hour of light activity. Spend any number of Hit Dice (each = roll the die + CON_mod, regain that many HP). Long rest: 8 hours, of which up to 2 hours may be light activity, none of it combat or strenuous. Regain all HP and half total Hit Dice (minimum 1). A creature must complete a long rest before benefiting from a second one in the same 24 hours.

entries.name: Rule: Death Saving Throws
entries.content: Death saving throws: at the start of your turn at 0 HP, roll d20. 10 or higher: success. Below 10: failure. Three successes: stable (unconscious but no longer dying). Three failures: dead. A natural 20: regain 1 HP. A natural 1: counts as two failures. Taking damage at 0 HP: one automatic failure (or two if the damage is a critical hit, or instant death if the damage equals or exceeds your HP maximum).

entries.name: Sub-Agents — what they do and how to enable them
entries.content:
Besides the main Ruleset Helper, the bundle installs a small consolidated pool of sub-agents. IMPORTANT: installing the bundle does NOT activate them — like all custom agents on Marinara 2.4.3+, they must be ENABLED FOR EACH GAME at load time, after the game launches (Marinara -> Settings -> Agents, or the game's agent selection). The ruleset's lorebook must ALSO be attached to the game (during game setup or after launch) — without it the agents have no ruleset rules to follow and will not work correctly.

The pool: combat-overseer (one pre-generation agent covering combat-math framing AND NPC roster tracking). context-fuser (one pre-generation agent covering rules-question answers AND current player-state reminders). state-mutator (the ONLY agent that changes the character sheet — it emits hidden [mrr-state: ...] tags the extension applies; covers HP, spell slots, conditions, inventory, death saves, XP).
pre-input-transformer (pre-generation; recasts player input in this system's vocabulary before the GM sees it).

Each enabled agent costs one extra model call per turn; on a provider that allows only one call at a time, every agent call runs one after another — enable only what your table needs. Enable state-mutator if you want narration to drive the sheet automatically; it is the sole writer, and with it off, sheet changes are manual.

entries.name: Mechanic: Magic Item Attunement
entries.content:
Magic item attunement (SRD 5.1). Many magic items require attunement — a one-hour focused process during a short rest — before the wielder can access the item magical properties. A creature can be attuned to at most 3 magic items at once; attempting a 4th attunement requires breaking an existing attunement first. Some items grant their basic effect without attunement (a +1 sword) but lock their full effect behind it (a magic sword that flames on command). Attunement breaks immediately on death, on the item leaving the wearer for 24 hours, or by deliberate choice during a short rest.

State-mutator tag: [mrr-state: field="attunement" item="<exact item name>" attuned="true"] to attune (cap-3 enforced; rejected with toast on overflow). attuned="false" to release. Items must already exist on the player inventory; emit an inventory add tag first if needed.

entries.name: XP Awards
entries.content:
(Progression mode lives in the always-on "XP Progression Mode" entry)

D&D 5e (SRD 5.1) experience awards. Set the line above to "Progression: milestone" to disable all GM-driven XP awards below — the party then levels up manually, at the table's discretion, whenever the story calls for it.

COMBAT — monster XP by Challenge Rating (award the sum for every creature defeated, neutralized, or meaningfully overcome in an encounter; split evenly is a table option, not a rule — this reference gives the total budget):
CR 0: 10 XP · CR 1/8: 25 XP · CR 1/4: 50 XP · CR 1/2: 100 XP · CR 1: 200 XP · CR 2: 450 XP · CR 3: 700 XP · CR 4: 1,100 XP · CR 5: 1,800 XP · CR 6: 2,300 XP · CR 7: 2,900 XP · CR 8: 3,900 XP · CR 9: 5,000 XP · CR 10: 5,900 XP. Higher CRs continue the same DMG progression; use the closest banded value below the encounter's actual CR total when no exact monster stat block is in play (a GM ruling, not a fabricated stat block).

SOCIAL / MENTAL / RP PARITY — award equivalents at CR-equivalent value so play is never "grind rats to level" (Corey's ruling 3, modeled on PF2e's accomplishment-XP pattern):
- Minor social/mental win (a skill challenge step succeeds, a clue is found through deduction, a minor NPC is won over): 25-100 XP, CR-1/8-to-CR-1/2 band.
- Moderate social/mental win (a negotiation concludes, a puzzle is solved, an investigation resolves): 100-450 XP, CR-1/2-to-CR-2 band.
- Major social/mental win (a faction is turned, a mystery's core truth is uncovered, a defining RP scene resolves a personal arc beat): 450-1,100 XP, CR-2-to-CR-4 band.
A costly or partial failure that still moves the story forward earns the LOW end of the matching band — failure is not automatically zero XP if it was consequential and well-played.

SESSION-END OPTION (a table may use this INSTEAD of or IN ADDITION to per-event awards, GM's call, noted once at session start): a flat 100-300 XP per player per session, scaled to session length and how much happened.

PARTY AWARDS — ruling 6, no party imbalances: every combat/social/RP/session award above applies to the WHOLE PARTY, not just the acting character. See the ruleset's state-mutator agent for the party target= emission mechanism — one award tag per PC roster member, same amount, NPCs never awarded.

Manual override always available: the player's XP/level sheet fields and the "+1 XP" button remain player-editable regardless of GM awards.

entries.name: Level-Up Procedure
entries.content:
D&D 5e (SRD 5.1) level-up procedure. Walk the player through these steps, in order, once XP crosses the threshold on their sheet's XP card (level 1-20 ladder, SRD default):

1. **Hit Points**: either take the fixed average for the class Hit Die (rounded up: d6=4, d8=5, d10=6, d12=7) or roll the die fresh — player's choice, consistent per campaign if the table prefers. Add Constitution modifier. Once the player confirms the roll/average, the State Mutator updates max HP directly with [mrr-state: field="Hit Points" max="<new max HP>" reason="Level <N> max HP: <die result/average> + CON mod"] — a max= write raises the ceiling; it does not touch current HP, so a separate hp= tag is only needed if the narration also restores/changes current HP this turn (e.g. a long rest to full).
2. **Proficiency Bonus**: check whether the new level crosses a proficiency-bonus breakpoint (levels 5, 9, 13, 17) and update if so.
3. **Class Features**: consult the class's level-by-level feature list (see the Class: <name> lorebook entries) for anything gained at the new level — extra attacks, new spell slots, class-specific resources, subclass features at the class's subclass-gain level.
4. **Ability Score Improvement / Feat**: at levels 4, 8, 12, 16, and 19 the character gets an ASI (+2 to one ability, or +1 to two, cap 20) or a feat, player's choice — mentioned here, NOT automated; the player decides and the GM confirms the pick before it's written to the sheet.
5. **Spell Slots / Prepared Spells** (casters only): advance per the class's spell slot table for the new level; prepared casters (Cleric, Druid, Wizard-prepared) recompute how many spells they can prepare (spellcasting ability modifier + class level, or per class rule); known casters (Sorcerer, Bard, Ranger, Warlock) may learn a new spell per their class table — player confirms each pick, nothing is auto-selected.

Once every applicable step above is confirmed with the player, the State Mutator emits ONE absolute tag: [mrr-state: field="xp" current="<total>" level="<new level>" next="<next threshold>" reason="Levelled up to <N> — <one-line summary of what changed>"]. HP/slot/feature changes ride their own normal state-mutator fields (hp, spellSlotN, etc.) alongside it, each citing what the player confirmed.

XP THRESHOLD LADDER (SRD 5.1 — AUTHORITATIVE for all level math; matches the sheet's XP table; use THIS, never memory, for any multi-level XP calculation):
L1:0 L2:300 L3:900 L4:2,700 L5:6,500 L6:14,000 L7:23,000 L8:34,000 L9:48,000 L10:64,000 L11:85,000 L12:100,000 L13:120,000 L14:140,000 L15:165,000 L16:195,000 L17:225,000 L18:265,000 L19:305,000 L20:355,000. A character is the highest level whose threshold their total XP meets or exceeds. 'Reach level N' means total XP = L<N>'s number exactly.
